The proposed WB HOME Project components are:
Component 1: Support for refugee housing subsidies focuses on providing housing solutions to eligible beneficiaries.
Subcomponent 1.1: Temporary rental subsidies through cash assistance: This subcomponent will finance the provision of cash assistance to eligible beneficiaries supported by the ongoing SAP in the form of direct cash transfers to about 44,508 eligible beneficiaries to cover rent, utilities, and other living costs. Assistance to the eligible beneficiaries will be provided through the GoAs past (reimbursement through retroactive financing) and ongoing cash support provided through the SAP.
Subcomponent 1.2: Subsidies for the acquisition of housing solutions: This subcomponent will finance direct subsidies to approximately 6,500 eligible refugee HHs under the HSP for the acquisition of housing solutions through participating commercial banks.
Subcomponent 1.3: Institutional Development in Housing: The subcomponent will finance procurement of goods, consulting, and non-consulting services for technical assistance (TA), advisory, and capacity building.
Component 2: Housing Finance Market Development provides liquidity to National Mortgage Company (NMC) to enhance its ability to refinance affordable mortgages under the HSP.
Component 3: Project Management will finance project management costs, communications and outreach activities, institutional strengthening and capacity building of the MLSA, and monitoring and evaluation activities.

description.narrative:
Facing increased spending pressures, the Armenian government sought additional financing from the international community for long -term integration of NK refugees. The government is exploring longer-term housing solutions for refugees that ensure equitable treatment for the host community and is working to harmonize pension payments, social benefits, long term housing for refugees with those of the host community. In response, the GCFF promptly added Armenia as its seventh Benefiting Country and approved the first grant.
In Dec 2024 Sida decided to contribute SEK 30,000,000 to the Global Concessional Financing Facility to provide concessional finance for middle income countries hosting refugees, with direct relevance to Armenia's housing response through ADB's THRIVE (USD 250 million, Result based loan) and the World Banks HOME (USD 250m, IPF with Performance Based Conditions). 2025 amendment added SEK 20,000,000 in 2025, bringing Sweden's total to SEK 50,000,000 funds are pooled within GCFF.
The GCFF responds to evolving country contexts and refugee situations in Armenia. The GCFF continued to support the regularization of refugees and their inclusion in national service delivery systems. In Armenia, it supported swift policy action to regularize the status of newly arrived refugees, providing them with the right to work and access social benefits and services. In Armenia refugees have to obtain citizenship to be eligible to apply for housing under GCFF to address long term inclusion into society.
Transformative Housing Reforms for Improved Vitality and Empowerment (THRIVE) Program by ADB - 30MSEK approved by Sida in 2024 Dec to contribute toward financing and addressing the long-term, sustainable housing needs of NK refugees. ADBs loan will finance mortgages and rental subsidy schemes for vulnerable group. The development of Armenia's housing finance sector is essential for the countrys economic growth, poverty reduction, and inclusiveness goals. In support of the governments housing program under Decree N 710-L and its broader social housing policy objectives, ADBs loan will finance mortgages and rental subsidy schemes for vulnerable groups. THRIVE will improve the social housing governance policy framework, establish resilient and inclusive housing finance systems, improve market regulations and financing mechanisms, strengthen institutions and enhance the financial knowledge of its beneficiaries. Specific key initiatives supported under the program include the harmonization of social benefits; a long-term strategy to address emerging housing needs; seismic resilience of the homes of beneficiaries; livelihood and economic opportunities, including for households headed by women; the participation of Armenian private commercial banks; and strengthening capital markets to raise financing from institutional investors in the private sector.
On 11 Sep 2025, ADB announced about THRIVE, approved a results-based loan to support Armenia's social housing policy thorough a press release.
On 30 Oct 2025 the Republic of Armenia (RA) and the Asian Development Bank signed THRIVE loan agreement.
On 16 Dec 2025, the Parliament of Armenia ratified THRIVE loan agreement between ADB and RA.
On 19 Dec 2025, the President of Armenia signed the Law on ratification of the loan agreement signed on October 30, 2025 between the Republic of Armenia and the Asian Development Bank for Housing Reform for Vitality Improvement and Empowerment (THRIVE) program.
